QuestionStmt.S: Three vectors $\hat{i} - \hat{k}$, $\lambda\hat{i} + \hat{j} + (1-\lambda)\hat{k}$ and $\mu\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + (1+\lambda-\mu)\hat{k}$ represents coterminous edges of a parallelepiped, then the volume of the parallelepiped depends on

Solution.S:
Volume of parallelepiped = $|[\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}]|$.

$$\vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{k}, \quad \vec{b} = \lambda\hat{i} + \hat{j} + (1-\lambda)\hat{k}, \quad \vec{c} = \mu\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + (1+\lambda-\mu)\hat{k}$$

$$V = \left| \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ \lambda & 1 & 1-\lambda \\ \mu & \lambda & 1+\lambda-\mu \end{vmatrix} \right|$$

Apply $C_3 \to C_3 + C_1$:

$$V = \left| \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ \lambda & 1 & 1 \\ \mu & \lambda & 1+\lambda \end{vmatrix} \right| = 1$$

Thus, the volume is constant (1), independent of both $\lambda$ and $\mu$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\text{neither }\lambda \text{ nor }\mu}$$

Hence, the correct option is D.
